details:
- CVE-2024-56337: start the server JVM with -Dsun.io.useCanonCaches=false,
  which completes the CVE-2024-50379 fix on case-insensitive file systems
  with Java 8 and 11
- CVE-2026-65927: restart the rewrite rules at the first rule, not at the
  second one, after a rule with the [N] flag matched, so earlier rules such
  as [F] are applied to the rewritten URL; reject the request with a 500
  response after 1000 [N] rounds
- CVE-2026-41293: validate HTTP/2 request header field names and values and
  reset the stream when they contain characters that are not allowed
- CVE-2026-55957: use a simple bind when the JNDIRealm validates a password by
  binding as the user, so a realm configured for GSSAPI no longer accepts any
  password
- CVE-2026-101296: use that simple bind for any other configured SASL
  mechanism as well (for example EXTERNAL), which also accepted any password
- CVE-2026-65182: select the security constraint with the longest matching path
  when one collection has several matching patterns
- CVE-2026-68569: fail authentication in the DataSourceRealm and JDBCRealm when
  the user does not exist (CLIENT-CERT, SPNEGO) or a database lookup fails
- CVE-2026-68763: remove a reset HTTP/2 stream from the connection flow control
  backlog and return its unused allocation to the connection window
- CVE-2022-29885: state in the documentation that the EncryptInterceptor does
  not make it safe to run clustering over an untrusted network
- CVE-2024-23672: close a WebSocket connection when the client does not answer
  the close message of the server within a timeout (30 seconds by default),
  so a client can no longer keep the connection open
- CVE-2026-29146: reject insecure EncryptInterceptor cipher modes and padding
  combinations, and warn that AES/GCM/NoPadding should be used instead of the
  CBC default that is open to a padding oracle attack
- CVE-2026-41284: limit WebDAV LOCK and PROPFIND request bodies to 4096 bytes
  by default (new maxRequestBodySize init parameter)
- CVE-2024-38286: handle TLS 1.3 key updates received while reading, and
  close the connection when too many handshake messages wait to be sent, so
  a client can no longer exhaust memory through the TLS handshake
- CVE-2026-93446: clear the NIO TLS handshake wrap flag when a connection is
  reused and after every write, so TLS 1.3 connections do not fail
  intermittently
- CVE-2024-34750: count each HTTP/2 stream out of the active streams exactly
  once, also when it is reset or its headers are rejected, so connections
  are no longer kept open with an infinite timeout
- CVE-2024-24549: reset an HTTP/2 stream at the end of the frame in which its
  headers exceed a configured limit, not after all headers were received
- CVE-2024-50379: lock a resource path while it is looked up, written or
  deleted, so a concurrent read and upload of the same file can no longer
  bypass the case sensitivity checks and have it run as a JSP
- CVE-2024-52316: set a 500 status when the JASPIC ServerAuthContext throws
  an AuthException, so the request can no longer pass authentication
- CVE-2025-24813: delete the partial PUT temporary file after the request,
  also when the upload fails, and create it with a random name rather than
  one derived from the request path
- CVE-2025-31651: handle percent-encoded and literal ';' and '?' characters in
  rewritten URLs so crafted requests can no longer bypass rewrite rules; take
  path parameters out of the rewritten URL before it is mapped
- CVE-2025-48989: count every HTTP/2 stream reset sent by the server towards
  the connection overhead limit (made you reset attack); also count DATA
  frames sent with async I/O, so valid connections are not closed early
- CVE-2025-55752: decode the rewritten URL before normalizing it, so rewrite
  rules can no longer be used to reach /WEB-INF/ or /META-INF/; fix QSA and
  QSD handling
- CVE-2026-59083: keep a literal '+' in a rewritten URL instead of decoding it
  to a space
- CVE-2025-66614: reject TLS requests whose host name and SNI host name map to
  different SSLHostConfig entries (new strictSni Connector attribute, on by
  default), closing a client certificate authentication bypass
- CVE-2026-32990: match the protocol host name case-insensitively in the
  strict SNI check
- CVE-2026-65637: apply the strict SNI check to HTTP/2 requests without
  :authority, using the host header; reject requests that have neither
